🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
pkg/operator/starter.go (1)
`563-571`: _📐 Maintainability & Code Quality_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Use the shared condition constant instead of a hardcoded literal.** The regexp pattern hardcodes `"NodeControllerDegraded"` as a string literal, while `starter_test.go` references the same condition type via `condition.NodeControllerDegradedConditionType` from `github.com/openshift/library-go/pkg/operator/condition`. Building the regexp from that constant avoids drift if the condition name ever changes and keeps production code and tests in sync on the same source of truth.
♻️ Proposed refactor ```diff + condition "github.com/openshift/library-go/pkg/operator/condition" + func newDegradedInertia() status.Inertia { return status.MustNewInertia( 2*time.Minute, status.InertiaCondition{ - ConditionTypeMatcher: regexp.MustCompile(`^NodeControllerDegraded$`), + ConditionTypeMatcher: regexp.MustCompile("^" + regexp.QuoteMeta(condition.NodeControllerDegradedConditionType) + "$"), Duration: 10 * time.Minute, }, ).Inertia } ```
Note that a prior similar change in `cluster-etcd-operator` received the same feedback that an exact-match matcher would ideally not require regex at all, though that was noted as a non-blocking future improvement.
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@pkg/operator/starter.go` around lines 563 - 571, The regexp in newDegradedInertia is hardcoding the NodeControllerDegraded condition name, which should come from the shared condition.NodeControllerDegradedConditionType constant instead. Update the ConditionTypeMatcher construction to use that constant as the source of truth so starter.go stays aligned with starter_test.go and any future condition renames. Keep the existing matcher behavior otherwise. ```
